A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LiteGS, with a shared framework and substantial revisions. All pages, equations, tables, algorithms and figures are readable and support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original Mip-NeRF 360 training-time and reconstruction-quality results, GPU profiling, and cache and tile-size analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction and timing results across three datasets, model-budget comparisons, rasterizer benchmarks and component ablations.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a one-warp-per-tile rasterizer with scanline computation, mixed precision and integer-based reduction, substantially revising v1's shared-memory multibatch reduction. It also introduces opacity-gradient-variance densification and opacity decay. Morton-based clustering, culling and compaction are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates reconstruction only on Mip-NeRF 360. v2 retains that dataset and adds actual evaluations on Tanks & Temples and Deep Blending, substantially broadening scene coverage.

E2.justification: v1 compares training times against 3DGS and its TamingGS-integrated variant, but reconstruction quality only against 3DGS. v2 Table 1 adds Mini-Splatting, Mini-Splatting v2, 3DGS-MCMC and SSS, and includes TamingGS variants in quality comparisons. Table 3 additionally evaluates the TC-GS tensor-core rasterizer.

E3.justification: v1 reports A100 and RTX3090 experiments; v2 uses RTX3090 only and introduces turbo, balance and quality model-budget regimes. These use 18K or 30K iterations, with a 40K Tanks & Temples comparison matching SSS. New rasterizer comparisons control Garden primitive counts at 500K, 2000K and 5728K.

E4.justification: v1's warp-stall profiling, cache-hit curves, patch-count analysis and tile-size comparison are no longer reported. v2 adds culling ablations measuring end-to-end time and quality, controlled rasterizer comparisons, and separate removal of opacity decay and the variance criterion, including their joint removal (Tables 2–4). These substantially change the component-level evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's opacity-gradient variance is an algorithmic criterion, not uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: v1's per-scene quality scores and two-GPU training times are replaced by dataset-level results for multiple budgets, with additional primitive counts and ablation outcomes. For example, v2 Table 1 reports Mip-NeRF 360 PSNR/time of 27.70 dB/145 s for turbo and 28.25 dB/515 s for quality. These are new results under revised settings, not established same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's compositing equation, v2 adds a scanline quadratic decomposition, explicit gradient formulation, and the new densification definition C_i times Var = S_i minus M_i squared divided by C_i. These substantially expand the mathematical specification of the method. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes modularity, dual APIs, preservation of the original 3DGS algorithm, 3.4x acceleration and approximately 30% lower memory use. v2 replaces this emphasis with system-and-algorithm codesign, parameter efficiency, up to 13.4x acceleration and state-of-the-art reconstruction quality. The title additionally introduces a subminute-training claim.

C2.justification: v2 introduces substantive explanations distinguishing unconverged regions from under-reconstructed regions through gradient variance, and explains opacity decay as reducing reset instability. It discusses register-pressure tradeoffs, attributes weaker lightweight LPIPS to lost high-frequency detail, and identifies Morton sorting's neglect of primitive size and anisotropy as a limitation. v1's attribution of Adam acceleration primarily to fusion disappears.

D1.justification: v2 adds detailed FP16/half2 choices, integer warp-reduction steps, Morton quantization and sorting instructions, four-pixels-per-thread configuration, and explicit densification and opacity schedules. v1's dual-API/autograd documentation and disclosure of adjusted SfM processing are absent. Both versions retain the same code repository URL.

R1.justification: The research positioning shifts from a modular library supporting diverse 3DGS extensions toward acceleration and densification. v2 adds substantial discussion of error-guided and color-guided densification, Mini-Splatting, TC-GS and other acceleration approaches, while removing much of v1's blur, dynamic-scene, anti-aliasing and gsplat-usability discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method and evaluation are extensively rewritten. v1's separate Motivation section is absorbed into the new narrative, and v2 introduces contribution bullets, dedicated ablation discussion and a conclusion. The title, author list and terminology also change.

P2.justification: The layout changes from single-column to two-column. v1's positioning schematic and profiling charts are replaced by paired quality–budget/time plots and a pipeline illustration. Results are reorganized into a multidataset comparison and component-analysis tables, and the two original pseudocode displays are replaced by a scanline algorithm.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited validation: Tables 1–4 compare speed, quality and model size against broader alternatives and test component contributions across three datasets. This provides much stronger evidence for the framework's effectiveness. These gains outweigh the loss of A100 results and detailed profiling, although reporting weaknesses remain: Table 1's caption gives 0.780 SSIM where Table 2 gives 0.870 for the corresponding setting, and the subminute title is unsupported by the reported 108–145 s turbo training times.
